paras: The whitecap shooting on the Day place was an attack in June 1903 in which unidentified men described as whitecaps fired into the homes of two Black families on the Day place in Amite County, Mississippi, wounding an elderly Black man. No arrests were reported, and Mississippi papers carried the attack as a sign that whitecapping had "again broke loose" in the county.

Both original reports presented the shooting as one more in a run of whitecap attacks in Amite County, the Brandon News calling it "another whitecapping escapade" there. A Jackson dispatch blamed the new outbreak on "a fresh agitation of the negro question" in the county, without saying what that agitation was.

According to a special dispatch from Jackson dated June 22, unknown parties fired several shots into the houses of two Black families on the Day place, and during the melee an old man was seriously wounded. Three days later the Brandon News gave a fuller account of what appears to be the same attack, naming the man shot as John Hiram and saying he was hit in the arm but escaped serious injury. That paper counted seventy-five bullet holes in the walls of his house and seventy-two empty Winchester shells and numerous tracks outside.
At a second Black family's place nearby, the Brandon News said, the whitecaps contented themselves with tearing down sixty panels of fence.

The Jackson dispatch stated that the authorities were making an investigation, but no report of arrests, an indictment or a trial appears in the coverage. In February 1904 the Atlanta Independent wrote that Black laborers had steadily left Amite, Franklin and Lincoln counties because of whitecapping, leaving the three counties short of most of the labor they needed.

The Hattiesburg Daily Progress ran the Jackson special on June 22 under the headline "White Caps Break Loose," and the Atlanta Constitution printed the same text a week later as "More Whitecaps in Amite." A condensed version appeared in the Water Valley Progress on June 27. Between July 1 and July 4 the paragraph circulated in Mississippi state-news columns as "The Whitecaps Again," with "last week" added, in The Leader, the Hernando Times-Promoter, the Scranton Chronicle, the Grenada Sentinel, the Macon Beacon and the Woodville Republican.

The white papers treated the attack as a brief item of state news, calling it a "depredation" or an "escapade" and offering no comment on the victims. No Black-press report of this incident was found; the Atlanta Independent's later editorial instead addressed whitecapping in the region generally, charging "white men" with lawless conduct "under the gulse of enforcing law and order."

The two original reports differ on the wound: the Jackson dispatch called the old man "seriously wounded," while the Brandon News said John Hiram escaped serious injury. They also differ on the second household, which the dispatch says was fired into and the Brandon News says lost only its fence, and neither names the other's victim or place, so their identification as one attack rests on timing and location.

reader.title: Whitecap shooting on the Day place, Amite County, Mississippi
bases: Every report attributes the shooting to 'whitecaps' acting against Black households in Amite County, described as a renewed outbreak of such attacks (A2, A3).

The Jackson special (A2) and the separately sourced Brandon News item (A3) agree that whitecaps fired into a Black home in Amite County in mid-June and wounded a man, though A3 names no place and differs on the severity of the wound, so the match is inferred.

accounts.label: Jackson special / state-news paragraph
accounts.gist: Unknown parties fired several shots into the houses of two Black families on the Day place and seriously wounded an old man; the outbreak was blamed on renewed agitation of 'the negro question' and the authorities were investigating.

accounts.label: Brandon News item
accounts.gist: Whitecaps fired into John Hiram's house, hitting him in the arm without serious injury, leaving 75 bullet holes and 72 Winchester shells; at a neighbor's place they only tore down sixty panels of fence.

framing.detail: Brief state-news paragraphs under headlines such as 'White Caps Break Loose' and 'The Whitecaps Again', calling the attack a 'depredation' and blaming 'a fresh agitation of the negro question'.
The Brandon News called it 'another whitecapping escapade' in Amite County, without comment on the victims.
The Atlanta Independent did not report this incident, but months later blamed 'the lawless conduct' of 'white men' whitecapping for an exodus of Black labor from Amite and neighboring counties.

versions.value: John Hiram 'hit in the arm, but escaped serious injury'

conflicts.note: Neither report names the other's victim, so the two may not describe the same man; A3 gives more physical detail, A2 is the more widely reprinted dispatch.

info: Shortly before June 22, 1903 (the Jackson dispatch date); the July reprints say 'last week' only because they recycled the paragraph
Two Black families on the Day place; 'an old negro' seriously wounded (A2); the Brandon News names the man shot as John Hiram (A3)
